## 3\. Why the CSS/classical-eroder construction does not yet close

The natural alternative is to construct one geometrically local CSS code with two compatible correction generators,

\[
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{corr}}
=
\sum_{i,\alpha}\mathcal D[X_i f_{i,\alpha}(S_Z)]
+
\sum_{i,\beta}\mathcal D[Z_i g_{i,\beta}(S_X)].
\]

The functions must use only bounded-radius syndrome information.

Drechsler, Oreg and Aharonov establish the precise reduction from syndrome-based Lindbladians to two classical error-sector processes. citeturn437766view3

Chakraborty and Lee establish an asynchronous stability criterion for certain monotone classical processes, using balanced stable directions, finite buffers and exponentially sparse coarse failures. citeturn124843view3

To combine these results into the requested theorem, one must actually exhibit a two- or three-dimensional CSS code with commuting checks and **both** induced sector processes satisfying an appropriate asynchronous memory theorem.

No such compatible pair is established by these two results.

There is an additional algebraic issue. Even a small allowed Hamiltonian perturbation,

\[
\mathcal E(\rho)=-i\epsilon[X_i,\rho],
\]

gives

\[
\mathcal E^*(Z_i)=2\epsilon Y_i.
\]

Thus arbitrary coherent perturbations generally do not preserve the diagonal or syndrome-based operator spaces underlying the exact classical reduction.

The inherited local-logical-safety lemma can control decoded logical drift without requiring sector closure. But it still needs control of the actual evolving unsafe-syndrome occupation.

Consequently, neither combining the two classical papers nor applying the local-safety lemma produces the needed autonomous quantum threshold.

## 4\. Why the three-dimensional thermal route remains insufficient

For a geometrically local three-dimensional stabilizer Hamiltonian, nominal Davies-type dynamics can have exponentially long storage in the established thermal construction. citeturn947448academia24

The full perturbation model asks for more. Once the physical background depolarization is included, the nominal dynamics need not have the original Gibbs state as a fixed point. Arbitrary permitted perturbations can also destroy detailed balance and create coherences between syndrome sectors.

A Peierls estimate for an equilibrium distribution is therefore not a bound on the evolving state under
